card.description:
If you’re looking for a special place to build or grow your career, you’ve found it. Whether you’re an experienced professional, a recent college graduate or somewhere in between, IDEX is a place where you can apply your existing skills and learn new ones in an environment where you can make an impact.

With interesting opportunities in engineering, marketing, sales, supply chain, operations, HR, finance, and more across more than 40 diverse businesses around the globe, chances are, we have something special for you.

**LOCATION:** Remote with Travel

US Valve is growing rapidly, driven by critical customer demand in data center and other high-growth markets, creating increasingly complex new product development programs with multiple manufacturing paths. The Director, NPI Program Management & Manufacturing Launch will build and lead the function responsible for taking these programs from business case through stable production, whether manufactured at US Valve, at sister IDEX business units, through external supply chain partners, or through a hybrid model. The role ensures that product design, manufacturing processes, suppliers, supply chain, quality systems, and commercial launch mature together against one integrated plan.

This leader is the single point of accountability for integrated NPI execution and owns end-to-end program results, including schedule, budget, quality, supplier readiness, manufacturing readiness, launch readiness, and ramp performance. The role organizes Product Management, Engineering, Operations, Quality, Supply Chain, Sourcing, Sales, Finance, BU partners, and external suppliers under one plan. The Director ensures APQP and launch deliverables, including PPAP, PFMEA, DFMEA, control plans, MSA, capability studies, and first article inspections, are completed on time and to standard. Success isn't design release; it is demonstrating that the full value stream can repeatedly meet customer demand with the required quality, cost, and delivery performance.

The right leader is a builder and results driver with the technical and operational credibility to walk the factory floor, challenge supplier capacity, identify manufacturing constraints, and lead cross-functional recovery. This person establishes the PMO, sets objective gate criteria and metrics, holds functional leaders and partners accountable without direct authority, challenges unrealistic plans, and leads recovery when programs fall behind. The leader will model IDEX values of trust, team, and excellence and build a high-performing team that scales with the business.

**KEY RESPONSIBILITIES:**

***Build and Lead the Function***

* Build and lead the Program Management Office (PMO), including organizational structure, staffing plan, talent development, and succession for program and launch managers.
* Establish standard NPD governance—stage-gate/tollgate process, templates, operating cadence, and decision rights—aligned with the IDEX Operating Model.
* Define objective gate-exit criteria and recommend Go, Conditional Go, Hold, or Re-scope decisions based on demonstrated evidence.
* Own the NPD and launch portfolio; prioritize programs using 80/20 principles and align resources to the highest-value customer and growth opportunities.
* Lead executive-level business case, tollgate, and launch-readiness reviews, driving clear decisions on scope, investment, timing, and manufacturing path.

***IDEX Connected Growth and Cross-BU Leadership***

* Drive programs across multiple sister IDEX business units, leveraging IDEX connected growth strategies to share capacity, technology, capabilities, and supply chain.
* Organize and align BU partners, supply chain partners, and internal manufacturing teams into a single integrated execution plan for each program.
* Maintain one integrated critical path and one objective program status across product, supplier, tooling, manufacturing, quality, material, and customer workstreams.
* Lead make, buy, partner, intercompany, and contract manufacturing strategies, including location, capacity, Capex, tooling, staffing, and timing.
* Establish cross-BU agreements, roles, and communication cadences that ensure clear accountability for deliverables across sites and partners.
* Partner with Product Management, Engineering, Operations, Quality, Supply Chain, Sales, and Finance to align program strategy with BU and IDEX growth objectives.

***Quality Management and Launch Readiness Across Supply Chain Partners***

* Drive quality management across multiple supply chain partners, sister BUs, and internal sites to ensure consistent standards from development through production.
* Ensure APQP and product launch deliverables are completed on time and to standard, including PPAP, PFMEA, DFMEA, control plans, process flow diagrams, MSA, capability studies, and first article inspections.
* Partner with Quality and Supply Chain to qualify, develop, and audit suppliers and contract manufacturers, and drive corrective actions to closure.
* Lead launch-readiness and production-readiness gates, ensuring no program advances without required quality, validation, and capacity evidence.
* Separate product validation from production-rate validation; require evidence that the complete value stream can repeatedly achieve required volume, yield, quality, and delivery performance.
* Drive post-launch stabilization, ensuring yield, quality, and delivery targets are met before handoff to steady-state operations.

***Advanced Manufacturing and Capacity***

* Identify and drive advanced manufacturing processes, automation, and technologies needed to meet critical customer demand and scale production.
* Drive readiness of critical processes including welding and joining, filtration media and filter manufacturing, precision machining, assembly, automation, and production test.
* Lead capacity planning and implementation of new processes, including equipment selection, CapEx justification, facility changes, validation, and ramp plans.
* Partner with equipment providers, consultants, and IDEX sites to accelerate process development and transfer best practices.
* Champion design for manufacturability, lean, and continuous improvement in all new product introductions.
* Ensure process qualification, fixtures, tooling, controls, operator readiness, capacity, and rate trials are incorporated before design freeze and production release.

***Metrics, Visibility, and Results***

* Define and own program and launch KPIs, dashboards, and reporting that provide clear leadership visibility across BUs and partners.
* Identify risks early—schedule, resource, quality, sourcing, cost, capacity, and production readiness—and drive countermeasures and recovery plans.
* Challenge unrealistic timelines, resource assumptions, and commitments; escalate decisions and support needs to executive leadership.
* Deliver regular executive updates on portfolio status, risks, decisions, and results.
* Travel domestically and internationally up to 25% to support program execution, supplier engagement, site coordination, customer needs, and equipment-provider activities.
* Perform other related duties and support additional program, PMO, or business needs as assigned.

**KEY PERFORMANCE METRICS:**

* On-time milestone and launch attainment across the NPD portfolio.
* PPAP on-time completion and first-pass approval rate across internal sites, sister BUs, and supply chain partners.
* PFMEA, DFMEA, and control plan completion prior to required gates.
* Launch quality, including first-pass yield, PPM, and escapes at launch and 90 days post-launch.
* Ramp-to-rate performance, including time to target capacity and on-time delivery to customers.
* Critical manufacturing process readiness, including qualification and demonstrated capability for welding/joining, filtration manufacturing, machining, assembly, and test as applicable.
* Program budget, Capex, and product cost performance versus business case.
* Supplier and partner quality and delivery performance on launch programs.
* New product and IDEX-connected growth revenue enabled.
* PMO team capability, staffing, and retention.

**QUALIFICATIONS:**

* Proven leader who has built and scaled a PMO, NPD launch, or program management function in a manufacturing environment.
* undefined
* Deep experience with APQP and product launch deliverables, including PPAP, PFMEA, DFMEA, control plans, and production part qualification.
* Track record driving quality and launch execution across multiple supply chain partners, contract manufacturers, and internal sites.
* Experience identifying and implementing advanced manufacturing processes, automation, and capacity expansions to meet demanding customer ramps.
* undefined
* Demonstrated success leading across multiple business units in a matrixed organization; multi-BU or IDEX experience preferred.
* Strong business acumen in make-versus-buy, multi-site manufacturing, CapEx, tooling, cost, capacity, and risk decisions.
* Builds metrics, dashboards, and operating cadence that drive accountability and measurable results.
* Influential leader able to align executives, BU partners, and suppliers, and hold owners accountable without direct authority.
* Strong executive communicator who turns complex program information into clear decisions and actions.
* Experience with welding/joining, filtration, pneumatics, fluid handling, pumps, compressors, blowers, valves, electromechanical products, precision manufacturing, data center, thermal management, or engineered industrial components preferred.
* Lean, Six Sigma, or PMP certification preferred; working knowledge of the IDEX Operating Model and 80/20 a plus.
* Proficient with project management tools, dashboards, and Microsoft Office applications.

**EDUCATION AND/OR EXPERIENCE:**

* Bachelor’s degree in engineering, business, operations, supply chain, or a related field required; MBA or advanced degree preferred.
* 10+ years of program management, NPD, manufacturing launch, quality, or operations experience, including 5+ years leading teams, with experience in industrialization, supplier development, site transfers, and multi-site manufacturing.

**PHYSICAL DEMANDS:**

* While performing the duties of the job, the employee is required to move around and be still, use hands to finger, handle or feel objects, tools, or controls; reach with hands and arms; talk and hear.
* Employee will occasionally lift up to 35 lbs.
* Specific vision abilities required by the job include close vision, distance vision, color vision, peripheral vision, depth perception, and the ability to adjust focus.

card.description:
**Job Title:** Plant Manager

**FLSA:** Exempt

**Employment Type:** Full-Time

**Reports to:** VP of Operations

**Job Overview:**

The primary responsibilities include managing all day-to-day plant operations. Manage and lead a team of production and warehouse employees. Responsible to improve efficiency, cost, quality, and safety through both individual and team contributions.

**Essential Responsibilities**:

* Supervise all plant operations including production and warehouse departments.
* Coordinate departmental activities to fulfill sales orders, meet inventory requirements and deliver manufactured products in a timely fashion.
* Manage staff, prepare work schedules, and assign specific duties in production. Establish and implement departmental policies, goals, objectives, and procedures, conferring with other department directors as necessary.
* Maintains communication and coaching to employees on a daily basis to ensure they have the information to do their jobs and that they understand and adhere to the goals and direction of the company.
* Trains direct reports on operating procedures, quality standards, environmental, health and safety procedures, and company policies. Ensures compliance and sustainment of training to ensure a smooth operation.
* Determine staffing requirements, and participate in the recruiting process i.e., interview, hire and train new employees.
* Provides performance and daily corrective feedback to employees as needed. Writes direct reports performance reviews. Recommends raises next level of discipline and terminations to Director of Operations and Human Resources Manager.
* Respond to emergency department requests. Troubleshoot issues to determine cause and solution.
* Participate in all shifts as necessary to assure the department is streamlined.
* Collaborates with other departments on projects as needed.
* Communicate regularly with plant personnel to maintain a high level of morale.
* Perform all other duties as assigned.

**Minimum Requirements:**

* Familiarity with manufacturing environments, and ability to apply fundamental troubleshooting skills to technical problems.
* Familiarity with Continuous Improvement, LEAN, and six-sigma.
* Familiarity with meeting OSHA standards and leading a culture of safety first.
* Ability to manage multiple tasks, set priorities, identify and addresses problems and meet deadlines.
* Ability to work effectively with a wide array of personnel.
* Self-motivated with the ability to work independently in a fast-paced environment with changing priorities.
* Computer skills to include ERP system and Microsoft programs. Must be able to use computer programs to keep track of administrative tasks such as report writing, analysis of work orders, evaluations of production estimates and outputs.
* Excellent communication skills with the ability to talk with groups of employees as well as strong one-on-one communication skills to facilitate employee engagement.
* Must be committed to the success of the entire organization.

**Physical Requirements:**

Requirements include, but are not limited to:

* Works in both an office environment and a warehouse.
* Requires sitting, operating a computer keyboard, telephone, and other office equipment for extended periods of time.
* Must be able to stand and walk for prolonged periods of time as required to the walk-shop floor.
* Must be able to lift and carry up to 50 lbs.
* Must be able to perform repetitive motions such as reaching and grasping.

* The work environment is in a warehouse/production and temperatures inside vary between hot and cold based on the outside conditions.
* This is a fast-paced environment with constantly changing priorities.

**Education/Experience:**

* Bachelor’s Degree in Business Administration, Engineering, Supply Chain Management or related field required.
* 10+ years leading a team in a manufacturing environment.
* Experience in the plastic bottle industry, or in a manufacturing environment, is highly preferred
* Must be "hands-on" and assist in completing department goals as required.

**Competitive Benefits:**

* Medical, dental, and vision insurance premium.
* Employer-paid Life Insurance
* Employer Match
* Paid Vacation and Paid Sick
* Holiday Pay

***We are an Equal Opportunity/ Affirmative Action Employer and do not discriminate against applicants due to veteran status, disability, race, gender, gender identity, sexual orientation or other protected characteristics.***

The Director of Continuous Improvement will support the AAI (Automotive, Aerospace, and Industrial) vertical. The services are primarily warehousing operations for distribution and inbound to manufacturing operations.

card.title: Director, Operational Excellence
card.description:
Abbott is a global healthcare leader that helps people live more fully at all stages of life. Our portfolio of life-changing technologies spans the spectrum of healthcare, with leading businesses and products in diagnostics, medical devices, nutritionals and branded generic medicines. Our 122,000 colleagues serve people in more than 160 countries.

**Director, Operational Excellence**

We're advancing cancer care through innovative screening and diagnostic tests that help patients and healthcare providers make informed decisions before, during and after a cancer diagnosis. Our growing portfolio includes Cologuard®, Oncotype DX®, Cancerguard® and Oncodetect®, along with advanced genetic testing, supporting patients from cancer prevention and early detection through personalized treatment decisions and recurrence monitoring. We're focused on helping more people take action against cancer at its earliest, most treatable stages, so they can live longer, healthier lives.

This role is based on-site in Madison, WI.

**Position Overview**

Abbott is seeking a Director, Operational Excellence to lead the development, implementation, and sustainability of operational excellence practices across our Cancer Diagnostics operations.

This leader will partner closely with operations leadership and frontline teams to strengthen daily management practices, improve operational performance, and build a culture of continuous improvement and accountability.

**Key Responsibilities:**

* Lead the implementation of operational excellence practices that improve safety, quality, delivery, productivity, and cost performance.
* Establish and sustain tiered management routines, visual performance boards, standardized metrics, and structured performance reviews across hourly, daily, weekly, and monthly intervals.
* Partner with operations leaders to implement supervisor standard work, strengthen accountability, and develop consistent problem-solving and performance management practices.
* Apply Lean and Six Sigma methodologies to improve process flow, eliminate waste, reduce variation, and drive measurable operational results.
* Establish employee-driven improvement programs that encourage frontline participation, idea generation, and ownership of operational improvements.
* Lead change management efforts that ensure new processes are adopted, embedded into daily operations, and sustained over time.
* Collaborate with Operations, Quality, Engineering, Supply Chain, and other stakeholders to align improvement initiatives with business priorities.
* Lead and coach a team of operational excellence professionals while building continuous improvement capabilities across the broader organization.

**Minimum Qualifications**

* Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Science, Operations Management, Business, Supply Chain, or a related field with a minimum of 10 years of relevant experience; or Master's degree in a related field with a minimum of 8 years of relevant experience.
* Significant progressive experience in operations leadership, operational excellence, or continuous improvement within a manufacturing, laboratory, or complex operational environment.
* Demonstrated experience implementing and sustaining Lean practices, daily management systems, visual performance management, and structured problem-solving.
* Experience leading operational teams or working directly with frontline leaders to drive measurable performance improvements.
* Proven ability to lead organizational change, influence cross-functional stakeholders, and build accountability.
* Strong people leadership, coaching, analytical, and problem-solving capabilities.

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Direct leadership experience in manufacturing, laboratory, or other high-volume operations.
* Experience in regulated industries such as diagnostics, medical devices, pharmaceuticals, or healthcare.
* Lean Six Sigma Green Belt certification or equivalent practical experience.
* Experience implementing tiered management systems, supervisor standard work, and employee-driven continuous improvement programs.
* Demonstrated success sustaining operational improvements through frontline engagement and leadership ownership.

The base pay for this position is $149,300.00 – $298,700.00. In specific locations, the pay range may vary from the range posted.

card.description:
**About Site**
Catalent’s Madison, Wisconsin site is a state‑of‑the‑art biologics development and manufacturing facility supporting customers from research through early‑ and mid‑stage clinical production. Located at 726 Heartland Trail in Madison, the approximately 102,700‑square‑foot GMP facility specializes in mammalian cell line engineering, drug substance biomanufacturing, and biopharmaceutical development, utilizing flexible single‑use systems to enable rapid scale‑up and customization. The site is home to Catalent’s proprietary GPEx® and GPEx® Lightning technologies, which are used to generate high‑yielding mammalian cell lines for biologic therapies, and supports production scales ranging from 50 to 4,000 liters for clinical manufacturing. Following a $45 million expansion announced in 2025, the Madison site has significantly increased capacity, added new equipment, and created approximately 200 highly skilled biohealth jobs, further strengthening its role within Catalent’s global biologics network and Wisconsin’s growing life sciences ecosystem.
 
 
**Position Summary**
We have an opportunity for a Senior Manager - Biomanufacturing, Manufacturing Technical Operations to join our team. This role leads the Manufacturing Technical Operations organization, including Manufacturing Engineering, Manufacturing Compliance, Deviation Investigation, and Manufacturing Training. The position ensures safe, compliant, and reliable biomanufacturing operations while driving continuous improvement and technical excellence. The successful candidate will help strengthen workforce capability, reduce operational risk, and ensure sustainable preventive solutions across manufacturing operations.
 
 
Shift: Monday - Friday 8:00AM - 5:00PM
 
 
Location: Madison, WI
 
 
100% Onsite
 
 
**The Role**

* Lead, coach, develop, and evaluate leaders and technical professionals supporting Manufacturing Engineering, Compliance, Deviation Investigation, and Training.
* Establish clear goals, role accountabilities, performance expectations, succession plans, and development strategies for the organization.
* Provide organizational ownership for Manufacturing-based engineering support and technical response to process, equipment, materials, automation, documentation, and execution issues.
* Establish and govern a structured Rapid Response Team process that defines the problem, operational impact, containment, technical resources, decision ownership, recovery plan, communications, and escalation pathway.
* Provide leadership and oversight for Manufacturing deviation investigations, including investigation quality, aging, cycle time, right-first-time approval, and recurring-event reduction.
* Ensure investigations are fact-based and clearly distinguish event description, product and process impact, root cause, contributing factors, correction, corrective action, and preventive action.
* Establish Manufacturing Technical Operations as a key owner and contributor to process readiness, including batch production record review, dry runs, equipment readiness, material availability, qualification status, and execution-risk review.
* Ensure new equipment is transitioned into routine use with defined operational ownership, procedures, training, spare parts, maintenance, and troubleshooting strategies.
* Establish an integrated performance-management system using measures such as recurrence, recovery time, repeat failures, downtime, deviation aging, investigation right-first-time performance, corrective and preventive action aging and effectiveness, qualification progress, equipment reliability, open risks, and project delivery.
* Use performance data to establish priorities, allocate resources, escalate risk, and hold leaders accountable for outcomes.

**The Candidate**
**Minimum Requirements**

* Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Biotechnology, Biological Sciences, Biochemistry, or another relevant scientific or technical discipline required.
* Ten (10) or more years of relevant manufacturing, engineering, technical operations, Manufacturing Science and Technology, Quality, or related experience.
* Five (5) or more years of progressive leadership experience, including responsibility for technical professionals, people leaders, or manufacturing-support organizations.
* Demonstrated experience leading complex technical problem solving and operational recovery in a Good Manufacturing Practice manufacturing environment.
* Demonstrated experience with deviation investigations, corrective and preventive actions, change control, root-cause analysis, inspection readiness, and quality risk management.
* Advanced understanding of current Good Manufacturing Practice biopharmaceutical manufacturing, including upstream, downstream, solution-preparation, equipment, and support systems.
* Demonstrable leadership experience at Catalent (including but not limited to participation in Catalent‑sponsored leadership programs such as Next Generation Global Leaders, GOLD, LEAD Now, General Manager Excellence, and GROW) may be considered in place of external experience.

**Preferred Skills & Background**

* Advanced degree preferred.
* Experience in Good Manufacturing Practice biopharmaceutical manufacturing.

* Defined career path and annual performance review and feedback process.
* Diverse, inclusive culture.
* Potential for career growth on an expanding team within an organization dedicated to preserving and bettering lives.
* Competitive paid time off plus 8 paid holidays.
* Community engagement and green initiatives.
* Medical, dental, and vision benefits effective day one of employment.
* Tuition reimbursement.

**Catalent offers rewarding opportunities to further your career!**
Join the global drug development and delivery leader and help us bring over 7,000 life-saving and life-enhancing products to patients around the world. Catalent is an exciting and growing international company where employees work directly with pharma, biopharma and consumer health companies of all sizes to advance new medicines from early development to clinical trials and to the market. Catalent produces more than 70 billion doses per year, and each one will be used by someone who is counting on us. Join us in making a difference.

This option is reserved for individuals who require accommodation due to a disability. Resumes submitted to any Catalent employee by a third party agency and/or search firm without a valid written & signed search agreement, will become the sole property of Catalent. No fee will be paid if a candidate is hired for this position as a result of an unsolicited agency or search firm referral. Thank you.

If you receive any such request, DO NOT respond— it is a fraudulent request. Please forward such requests to spam@catalent.com for us to investigate with local authorities.
 
 
California Job Seekers can find our California Job Applicant Notice HERE.

Consistent with Massachusetts law, Catalent does not require or administer lie detector tests as a condition of employment or continued employment.

card.title: Director, Plant Operations
card.description:
Welcome to CTI Foods, where quality, service, and people are at the heart of everything we do. We are a leading food manufacturing company, dedicated to providing our customers with the best possible products and our employees with a rewarding career.
 
 
At CTI, we passionately believe that people are our #1 ingredient. We provide a positive and supportive work environment, opportunities for growth and advancement, and a competitive compensation package. We value our employees' contributions and strive to create a culture of respect, teamwork, and excellence.
 
 
Whether you're interested in a career in production, quality control, or management, we have a variety of opportunities available. We believe that our success is a result of our focus on quality, service, and people, and we look forward to continuing to serve our customers and employees with excellence.
 
 
If you're looking for a rewarding career in the food manufacturing industry, look no further than CTI Foods! Join our team and become a part of a company that values quality, service, and people.
 
 
**Job Overview**
To lead and direct production and maintenance functions for the respective location, while supporting and adhering to the efforts of safety, food safety, supply chain, human resources, and commercialization, in order to meet location’s business objectives as established by the Senior Leadership Team.
 
 
**Responsibilities**

* Direct daily operations while maintaining compliance to quality and regulatory standards.
* Execute all plans and initiatives as directed by safety, supply chain, food safety, HR and other cross functional areas.
* Achieve all location KPIs.
* Achieve budget for all operating costs including manufacturing, maintenance, and labor.
* Champion and model the CTI culture and the necessary mindsets to (3Fs) to deliver optimal results.
* Actively participate and engage with other plant leaders for best practice sharing and replication for areas such as network optimization and asset efficiency.
* Lead continuous improvement efforts around plant performance, people and processes to execute on current goals and to prepare for future growth.
* Lead team by effectively utilizing CTI’s Operating Principles.
* Attract, hire and lead the supervisory teams throughout the location, ensuring that all team members are knowledgeable with operating processes and procedures.
* Ability to develop the maintenance department into a pro-active / asset life management model.
* Identify, study and determine the processing equipment that best meets production needs from a product quality and productivity standpoint.
* Play a key role on major CAPEX project budgeting and large project management to ensure timely completion and on budget.
* Define and model the overall facility capacity to have an overall understanding of bottlenecks and limitations.
* Knowledge of USDA-FSIS regulations and ability to work with USDA inspectors on an ongoing basis to ensure compliance to all USDA regulations and HACCP and SQF requirements.
* Knowledge of other regulatory requirements, including OSHA and EPA/DNR. OSHA experience covering worker safety in a protein processing environment as well as ammonia-based refrigeration. EPA/DNR as it pertains to plant discharges either by air or water.
* Maintains continuity among work teams by documenting and communicating actions, irregularities, and continuing needs.
* Any other duties as assigned.

**Qualifications**
What we need from you:
 
 

* Minimum of 10 years of operations management experience, food manufacturing preferred. Bachelor’s degree in Business, Food Science, Engineering, or related field preferred.
* Ability to apply understanding to carry out instructions furnished in written, oral or diagram form.
* Track record of strong performance as a senior operations manager with demonstrated operations and management talent and a desire to participate in a team environment.
* Demonstrated experience in organizational and process improvement, ideally with using Lean, Kaizen, and Six Sigma concepts.
* Long term and short-term planning skills.
* Budget development and presentation skills.
* Ability to effectively analyze and evaluate new equipment and new processes and assign a value for reduced labor, yield improvement, or quality improvement.
* Negotiating strategy and skills, for dealing with vendors, union, or government personnel.
* Must be able to adapt to and become an advocate of the company mission and vision statements.
* Team member who will quickly earn and maintain the personal and professional respect of people inside and outside the Company.
* Articulate and effective communicator with the ability to influence others through the employment of sound judgment.
* Maintains professional demeanor, high standards of integrity, honesty, loyalty, and ethical values.

What you'll receive from us:
 
 

* Salary within the range of $160,000 - $175,000, depending on experience\*
* Unlimited PTO\*
* Medical, Dental, & Vision Insurance
* Company Paid Life Insurance
* Telehealth Services
* 401K Matching
* FSA & HSA available
* EAP and wellbeing support
* Tuition reimbursement program available
* The estimate displayed represents the typical salary range of candidates hired. Factors that may be used to determine your actual salary may include your specific skills, how many years of experience you have and comparison to other employees already in this role. Most candidates will start in the bottom half of the range. Unlimited PTO requests are subject to approval and is subject to the current business needs of CTI Foods.

Whether you’re an experienced professional, a recent college graduate or somewhere in between, IDEX is a place where you can apply your existing skills and learn new ones in an environment where you can make an impact.
 
 
With interesting opportunities in engineering, marketing, sales, supply chain, operations, HR, finance, and more across more than 40 diverse businesses (https://www.idexcorp.com/our-businesses/business-segments/) around the globe, chances are, we have something special for you.
 
 
**LOCATION:**
Remote with Travel
 
 
US Valve is growing rapidly, driven by critical customer demand in data center and other high-growth markets, creating increasingly complex new product development programs with multiple manufacturing paths. The Director, NPI Program Management & Manufacturing Launch will build and lead the function responsible for taking these programs from business case through stable production, whether manufactured at US Valve, at sister IDEX business units, through external supply chain partners, or through a hybrid model. The role ensures that product design, manufacturing processes, suppliers, supply chain, quality systems, and commercial launch mature together against one integrated plan.
 
 
This leader is the single point of accountability for integrated NPI execution and owns end-to-end program results, including schedule, budget, quality, supplier readiness, manufacturing readiness, launch readiness, and ramp performance. The role organizes Product Management, Engineering, Operations, Quality, Supply Chain, Sourcing, Sales, Finance, BU partners, and external suppliers under one plan. The Director ensures APQP and launch deliverables, including PPAP, PFMEA, DFMEA, control plans, MSA, capability studies, and first article inspections, are completed on time and to standard. Success isn't design release; it is demonstrating that the full value stream can repeatedly meet customer demand with the required quality, cost, and delivery performance.
 
 
The right leader is a builder and results driver with the technical and operational credibility to walk the factory floor, challenge supplier capacity, identify manufacturing constraints, and lead cross-functional recovery. The leader will model IDEX values of trust, team, and excellence and build a high-performing team that scales with the business.
 
 
**Key Responsibilities**
***Build and Lead the Function***

* Build and lead the Program Management Office (PMO), including organizational structure, staffing plan, talent development, and succession for program and launch managers.
* Establish standard NPD governance—stage-gate/tollgate process, templates, operating cadence, and decision rights—aligned with the IDEX Operating Model.
* Define objective gate-exit criteria and recommend Go, Conditional Go, Hold, or Re-scope decisions based on demonstrated evidence.
* Own the NPD and launch portfolio; prioritize programs using 80/20 principles and align resources to the highest-value customer and growth opportunities.
* Lead executive-level business case, tollgate, and launch-readiness reviews, driving clear decisions on scope, investment, timing, and manufacturing path.

***IDEX Connected Growth and Cross-BU Leadership***

* Drive programs across multiple sister IDEX business units, leveraging IDEX connected growth strategies to share capacity, technology, capabilities, and supply chain.
* Organize and align BU partners, supply chain partners, and internal manufacturing teams into a single integrated execution plan for each program.
* Maintain one integrated critical path and one objective program status across product, supplier, tooling, manufacturing, quality, material, and customer workstreams.
* Lead make, buy, partner, intercompany, and contract manufacturing strategies, including location, capacity, Capex, tooling, staffing, and timing.
* Establish cross-BU agreements, roles, and communication cadences that ensure clear accountability for deliverables across sites and partners.
* Partner with Product Management, Engineering, Operations, Quality, Supply Chain, Sales, and Finance to align program strategy with BU and IDEX growth objectives.

* Drive quality management across multiple supply chain partners, sister BUs, and internal sites to ensure consistent standards from development through production.
* Ensure APQP and product launch deliverables are completed on time and to standard, including PPAP, PFMEA, DFMEA, control plans, process flow diagrams, MSA, capability studies, and first article inspections.
* Partner with Quality and Supply Chain to qualify, develop, and audit suppliers and contract manufacturers, and drive corrective actions to closure.
* Lead launch-readiness and production-readiness gates, ensuring no program advances without required quality, validation, and capacity evidence.
* Separate product validation from production-rate validation; require evidence that the complete value stream can repeatedly achieve required volume, yield, quality, and delivery performance.

* Drive readiness of critical processes including welding and joining, filtration media and filter manufacturing, precision machining, assembly, automation, and production test.
* Lead capacity planning and implementation of new processes, including equipment selection, CapEx justification, facility changes, validation, and ramp plans.

At Lilly, the work is demanding because patients are waiting. Position Description
 
Sr. Manager Quality Assurance (QA) Parenteral is responsible for the staffing, training, and leadership of the quality assurance group supporting the project/expansion delivery, process development, operational readiness, start up, and validation/qualification of the parenteral process including dispensing, equipment preparation, formulation, filling and visual inspection. The Sr. Manager will help build a strong quality culture and lead the QA team for oversight and support of the ongoing operation as well as site inspection readiness and execution.
 
 
**On-site Shift Schedule:** Monday to Friday 0800-1630 until qualified and then will transition to 1800-0600 (2, 2, 3 schedule).
 
**Direct Reports:** Night shift team 6pm to 6am
 
 
Key Objectives / Deliverables
 

* The Night Shift Sr. Manager, Quality Assurance, will support the start-up and routine operation of the QA organization overseeing Parenteral operations at Lilly's Kenosha, Wisconsin pharmaceutical manufacturing site. Responsibilities include technical and administrative leadership, as well as project management.
* Serve as technical resource to review and approve technical documents
* Network with cross-functional technical project delivery team to ensure equipment and systems comply with quality requirements and are implemented with a Quality by Design framework
* Work with the Associate Director, Quality Assurance to support the development of the vision, strategy and quality culture for the overall site quality assurance organization with focus on the formulation, filling and visual inspection programs
* Support initial recruiting, build capability, for a diverse leadership and quality assurance staff to support qualification, validation and routine production
* Manage a team of up to approximately 8-12 direct reports
* Support the site to ensure a safe work environment including supporting and leading safety efforts for your team
* Support the development of the overall site operational readiness plan including development of quality processes and approval of operational procedures and controls
* Foster a strong quality culture including maintaining open communications and promoting teamwork and employee participation in the work group
* Supervise, coach, and aid in employee development and performance management; ensure a fair and equitable work environment
* Review and approve GMP documentation including procedures, deviations, technical reports, change controls, etc.
* Network with global and other parenteral sites to understand best practices and share knowledge

* Support inspection readiness activities
* Interact with regulatory agencies during inspections regarding cGMP issues
* Ensure data integrity by design

* 5+ years in pharmaceutical leadership including leading or working effectively with a cross-functional group
* Excellent interpersonal, written and oral communication skills
* Strong technical aptitude and ability to train and mentor others
* Ability to work overtime as required
* Ability to travel 10-25% to other Lilly sites for training/meetings
* May be required to respond to operational issues outside of core business hours and days

* Commit to successfully maintain Lilly Computer System Quality Assurance (CSQA) Certification
* Strong knowledge of Quality Management Systems and applicable regulatory requirements
* Previous experience directly supporting a pharmaceutical manufacturing operation
* Excellent interpersonal, written and oral communication skills
* Strong technical aptitude and ability to train and mentor others
* Demonstrated technical writing skills
* Demonstrated problem-solving and decision-making skills
* Previous facility or area start up experience
* Previous equipment qualification and process validation experience
* Previous experience with highly automated syringe filling, vial filling, and visual inspection equipment
* Previous experience with Manufacturing Execution Systems and electronic batch release
* CQM, CQE, or CQA certification from the American Society for Quality (ASQ)
* Previous experience with deviation and change management systems including Trackwise, MasterConrrol, and Veeva

card.description:
Req ID: 11315

**Working Location: District Columbia, Washington; Massachusetts, Westborough; Pennsylvania, Center Valley**

**Workplace Flexibility: Remote**

 

***For more than 100 years, Olympus has focused on making people’s lives healthier, safer and more fulfilling.***

Every day, we live by our philosophy, True to Life, by advancing medical technologies and elevating the standard of patient care so people everywhere can fulfill their desires, dreams, and lives.

Our five Core Values empower us to achieve Our Purpose:

**Patient Focus, Integrity, Innovation, Impact and Empathy.**

 

Learn more about Life at Olympus: https://www.olympusamerica.com/careers.

**Job Description**
-------------------

Senior Director, Regulatory & Quality Counsel, Global, reports to the VP, Regulatory & Quality Counsel, Global, and serves as a strategic legal partner to the Company's global Quality Assurance, Regulatory Affairs, and Medical Safety organizations. This role provides expert legal counsel on the full spectrum of medical device regulatory, quality, compliance, enforcement, and commercialization matters across the product lifecycle, including emerging technologies such as artificial intelligence (AI), software as a medical device (SaMD), digital health, and connected medical devices products.

Senior Director, Regulatory & Quality Counsel, Global will independently manage significant legal projects, advise leadership on complex regulatory risks, support interactions with FDA and global health authorities, lead legal support for regulatory inspections and enforcement actions, and provide strategic guidance on remediation programs, product development, commercialization, and global compliance initiatives. The role also provides leadership and oversight to other attorneys supporting the Global QARA organization.

This role covers multiple jurisdictions across the Americas, as well as other key business centers located in Japan, Europe, the Middle East and Africa, China, Asia Pacific.

**Job Duties**
--------------

* Strategic QARA Legal Support
 
 + Act as a strategic legal partner to Global Quality Assurance and Regulatory Affairs teams and business clients, providing practical, risk-based legal advice on regulatory, quality, compliance, and enforcement matters.
 + Provide day-to-day legal counseling to internal stakeholders on regulatory and quality matters affecting the development, manufacture, distribution, promotion, and post-market management of medical devices to support compliance with global medical device regulations.
* Global Regulatory Compliance
 
 + Counsel the business on all aspects of medical device regulation throughout the product lifecycle, including research and development, clinical activities, regulatory submissions, commercialization, post-market surveillance, quality systems compliance, and lifecycle management.
 + Assist business teams in obtaining FDA and other global regulatory clearances, approvals, registrations, licenses, and certifications necessary to market medical device products.
 + Support compliance with post-market regulatory requirements, including reporting obligations, field actions, recalls, and corrective actions.
 + Draft, review, and provide legal guidance regarding policies, procedures, quality system documentation, guidance documents, product manuals, training materials, and governance documents.
* Inspections, Enforcement, and Remediation
 
 + Advise the business regarding FDA inspections and inspections conducted by global regulatory authorities, including Notified Bodies, Health Canada, MHRA, PMDA, TGA, ANVISA, and other competent authorities.
 + Support inspection readiness activities, inspection management, inspector interactions, document production, escalation processes, and post-inspection response strategies. Provide legal advice regarding inspectional observations (e.g., Form 483 observations), warning letters, import alerts, recalls, detentions and import restrictions, regulatory investigations, and other enforcement actions by FDA and global health authorities. Advise and assist in drafting responses to inspectional observations, regulatory inquiries, Warning Letters, and other enforcement communications.
 + Provide strategic legal oversight for remediation and quality-system improvement programs arising from FDA or other regulatory authority findings.
* Import and Export Compliance
 
 + Advise on FDA and global medical device import and export requirements. Provide legal support regarding import-for-export requirements, import alerts, detentions, product admissibility issues, global distribution and supply chain activities, and resolution of import restrictions and enforcement actions.

**Job Qualifications**
----------------------

**Required:**

* Minimum of 10 years of legal experience supporting FDA-regulated medical device companies.
* Combination of in-house counsel, law firm, and/or regulatory agency experience, including FDA experience.
* Significant experience advising medical device businesses on regulatory, quality, compliance, and enforcement matters.
* Demonstrated experience counseling senior leadership regarding global recalls, FDA inspections, Form 483 observations, Warning Letters, Import Alerts, and other enforcement actions.
* Experience leading or advising on complex remediation programs arising from FDA or other regulatory authority findings.
* Experience supporting inspections and interactions with FDA and global regulatory authorities.
* Experience advising on medical device import/export requirements and regulatory trade compliance issues.
* Experience managing complex cross-functional legal and compliance initiatives in a global environment.
* Deep expertise in medical device regulatory and quality law.
* Strong understanding of FDA medical device requirements and global regulatory frameworks.
* Strong understanding of enforcement trends and evolving regulatory requirements affecting digital health and AI-enabled medical devices.

At Regeneron, we use science and innovation to develop life-changing medicines for people with serious diseases. We are seeking a Senior Manager, Global Development Quality Assurance to join our Global Development Quality Assurance (GDQA) team, supporting our Global Development (GD) organization. This position offers the opportunity to contribute to a fast-growing, science-driven organization making a meaningful difference to patients worldwide.

**When & where:**

Location: Tarrytown, NY
 
Work model: On-Site

**Discover your role:**

* This role may require 20 – 30% travel (both domestic and international).

card.description:
Futures start here. Where first steps, new friendships, and confident learners are born. At KinderCare Learning Companies, the first and only early childhood education provider recognized with the**Gallup Exceptional Workplace Award**, we offer a variety of early education and child care options for families. Whether it’s KinderCare Learning Centers, Champions, or Crème de la Crème, we build confidence for kids, families, and the future we share. And we want you to join us in shaping it—in neighborhoods, at work, and in schools nationwide.

At Crème de la Crème, learning comes alive like nowhere else. Our centers are places that never stand still because kids never do. And when you join us, you’ll become part of that magic—making a memorable impact on young learners and their families every day. In our wow-worthy world of learning, your talents will be the catalyst for creating child care experiences you've never imagined. You’ll link arms with other exceptional humans who care as much about helping kids reach their highest potential as you do—and you’ll know that your work matters.

* As the Crème School Director of Education and Quality, you will 
 + Lead and develop teachers to ensure curriculum alignment with best practices, state standards, and the individual needs of children.
 + Facilitate training and implementation of our comprehensive and developmentally appropriate curriculum for early childhood education.
 + Provide transformative leadership in the field of early childhood education, staying informed about current trends, research, and best practices.
 + Develop a culture of continuous learning and professional development while leading the teaching staff.
 + Establish and maintain high-quality standards for early childhood education program
 + Conduct regular assessments, evaluations, and audits to ensure compliance with Crème standards and licensing requirements
 + Provide guidance and support to teaching staff, promoting a positive and collaborative work environment. In partnership with the Executive Director, host professional development programs to enhance educators' skills and knowledge.
 + Cultivate positive relationships with teachers and parents, involving them in their child's education and development.
 + Collaborate with the community to enhance the educational experience and promote your school within the community.
 + Assist as needed in daily school operations, at times including direct supervision of children
 + Apply data-driven insights to assess program effectiveness, implement strategies to address identified areas of improvement, fostering a culture of continuous quality enhancement.
* Qualifications:
* + Bachelor’s degree in early childhood education, Education Administration, or a related field. (preferred)
 + Meet state specific credentials / guidelines for the role
 + At least one year leadership experience in early childhood education or a related field
 + Proven understanding of early childhood development, educational best practices, and program administration.
 + Excellent communication and interpersonal skills
 + Outstanding customer service skills, strong organizational skills, and multi-task and handle multiple situations optimally.
 + Proven ability to build and sustain positive relationships with diverse staff, families, and community. Commitment to diversity, equity, and inclusion in education.
 + Physically able to use a computer with basic proficiency, lift a minimum of 40pounds, and work indoors or outdoors.
 + Able to assume postures in low levels to allow physical and visual contact with children, see and hear well enough to keep children safe, and engage in physical activity.
 + Read, write, understand, and speak English to connect with children and their parents in English.

Range of pay $34,216.00 - $62,100.00 Salary

**Our benefits meet you where you are.** We’re here to help our employees navigate the integration of work and life: 

* Know your whole family is supported with **discounted child care** benefits.

* Breathe easy with **medical, dental, and vision** benefits for your family (and pets, too!).
* Feel supported in your mental health and personal growth with **employee assistance programs.**
* Feel great and thrive with access to **health and wellness programs, paid time off** and **discounts** for work necessities, such as cell phones.
* … and much more.

 
.

We operate research-backed, accredited, and customizable programs in more than 2,000 sites and centers across 40 states and the District of Columbia. As we expand, we’re matching the needs of more and more families, dynamic work environments, and diverse communities from coast to coast. Because we believe every family deserves access to high-quality child care, no matter who they are or where they live. Every day, you’ll help bring this mission to life by building community and delivering exceptional experiences. And if you’re anything like us, you’ll come for the work, and stay for the people.

*KinderCare Learning Companies is an Equal Opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, national origin, age, sex, religion, disability, sexual orientation, marital status, military or veteran status, gender identity or expression, or any other basis protected by local, state, or federal law.*

**Become a part of our caring community**
=========================================

Humana is committed to helping people achieve their best health by delivering innovative technology solutions that enable exceptional member and provider experiences.
 
 
The Director, Segment Quality Engineering is a strategic technology leader responsible for advancing quality engineering practices across a defined portion of Humana’s technology portfolio. Reporting to the AVP, Quality Engineering – Segment, this role will lead teams responsible for delivery quality, test automation, release readiness, and continuous improvement across multiple product and application teams.
 
 
This leader will work closely with Product, Engineering, Architecture, Platform, DevOps, and enterprise quality partners to embed quality throughout the software development lifecycle and improve release confidence, delivery speed, and production stability.

**Responsibilities**

 

* Lead quality engineering strategy and execution across a defined portfolio, domain, or segment.
* Lead and develop quality engineering managers, leads, engineers, and SDETs; drive organization design, talent growth, and team performance.
* Establish portfolio quality goals, KPIs, and governance to improve delivery quality, release readiness, and production stability.
* Embed built-in quality across planning, design, development, testing, and deployment.
* Oversee test strategy and execution across functional, integration, end-to-end, regression, and release validation.
* Own portfolio-level quality risk management, including defect trends, release concerns, environment issues, and cross-team dependencies.
* Drive automation-first practices and integrate quality signals, validation, and gates into CI/CD pipelines.
* Lead adoption of AI-enabled quality engineering capabilities and promote innovative practices that improve speed, coverage, and reliability.
* Sponsor modernization of quality frameworks, tooling, and test approaches for APIs, distributed systems, and cloud-native platforms.
* Oversee non-functional quality practices, including performance, resiliency, operational readiness, and security validation.
* Use metrics and production insights to drive continuous improvement, maturity, and investment priorities.
* Partner with segment and enterprise stakeholders to align execution with broader quality engineering strategy, standards, and reference architecture direction.
* Ensure responsible adoption of AI and compliance with applicable security, privacy, regulatory, and operational standards.

**Use your skills to make an impact**
=====================================

**Required Qualifications**

 

* Bachelor’s degree or equivalent experience.
* 10+ years of experience in software engineering, quality engineering, testing, or related technical disciplines.
* 5+ years of leadership experience managing quality engineering, test automation, or software delivery teams in large enterprise environments.
* Experience leading quality engineering execution across multiple agile teams or a complex application/product portfolio.
* Demonstrated success driving quality engineering modernization, including automation, tooling, process improvement, and metrics-driven execution.
* Strong understanding of Agile, DevOps, and CI/CD practices.
* Experience with API, UI, integration, regression, and end-to-end testing approaches.
* Familiarity with distributed systems and modern application architectures.
* Strong communication and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to influence cross-functional leaders.
* Experience working in matrixed organizations and leading geographically distributed teams.

**Preferred Qualifications**

 

* Experience in healthcare or another highly regulated industry.
* Familiarity with member, provider, digital experience, or enterprise platform domains.
* Experience with enterprise quality tools, test management platforms, and engineering lifecycle tools.
* Knowledge of microservices, APIs, event-driven systems, and cloud-native architectures.
* Experience supporting non-functional testing, including performance and resiliency.
* Exposure to AI-enabled quality engineering or intelligent automation capabilities.
* Familiarity with enterprise reference architecture principles, patterns, and standards in cloud, hybrid, on-premise, and SaaS environments.

**Success in this Role**

 

* In this role, success will be measured by:
* Improved release stability and delivery quality across the assigned portfolio.
* Reduced escaped defects and production incidents related to delivery quality.
* Increased automation adoption, regression reliability, and validation efficiency.
* Stronger integration of quality engineering into engineering workflows and CI/CD pipelines.
* Advancement of quality engineering maturity and consistent execution across teams.
* Positive stakeholder partnership and strong team engagement and development outcomes.

card.title: Senior Director, GMP Quality Assurance (Commercial)
card.description:
At Kailera, we are bold, authentic and committed to our mission of developing therapies that give people the power to transform their lives and elevate their overall health. Rooted in an entrepreneurial spirit and a team-oriented culture, we are working together to advance Kailera's mission to advance novel therapies for obesity and related conditions.
 
 
We are passionate about creating an inclusive workplace that promotes collaboration, integrity, and excellence. As we expand, we seek the most talented individuals with diverse backgrounds, cultures, perspectives, and experiences to join our team.

**What You'll Do:**

Kailera is preparing to bring its therapies to patients, and the Senior Director, GMP Quality Assurance will lead the quality strategy that gets us there. Reporting to the Head of Quality Assurance, you will be accountable for GMP Quality across drug substance, drug product, packaging/labeling, testing, stability, and product release as Kailera moves from late-stage clinical supply to commercial manufacturing and launch. You will develop and execute the commercial GMP Quality strategy, build the quality systems and team needed for a compliant and reliable commercial supply chain, and serve as a trusted quality leader with Technical Operations, Regulatory, Supply Chain, and our network of contract manufacturers and testing laboratories.

 

*Required location: Waltham, MA (hub-based, onsite 3-4 days per week) OR Remote (home-based, onsite at a hub 1 week every other month).*

 

**Responsibilities:**

* Develop and execute the commercial GMP Quality strategy and roadmap, aligned with company and functional objectives, to support registration, launch, and lifecycle supply of Kailera products
* Be accountable for the performance and results of the GMP Quality function, including key quality initiatives, goals, and product assets
* Evolve the Kailera Quality Management System from clinical phase to commercial readiness, including change control, deviations/CAPA, complaints, product quality reviews, supplier management, training, and data integrity
* Define GMP quality metrics and KPIs for Quality Management Review, and use trends to anticipate risks and drive continuous improvement across the manufacturing network
* Advise senior leadership on quality risks, compliance trade-offs, and changes in the global regulatory environment, translating external trends into Kailera's quality strategy
* Lead the quality aspects of commercial readiness, including oversight of process performance qualification (PPQ), process and analytical method validation, commercial specifications, and stability programs
* Lead pre-approval and pre-license inspection (PAI/PLI) readiness across Kailera and contract manufacturing sites; host or support health authority inspections and drive timely, effective responses and commitments
* Partner with Regulatory CMC to ensure commercial manufacturing and controls are consistent with marketing applications; provide QA review of CMC sections of regulatory filings, post-approval supplements, and variations
* Establish and oversee commercial batch record review and lot disposition, ensuring final disposition complies with approved registrations and supporting QP certification for EU supply
* Build post-market quality processes, including product complaint handling, regulatory reporting (e.g., Field Alert Reports), recalls, and annual product quality reviews.
* Oversee quality requirements for commercial packaging, labeling, artwork control, and serialization (DSCSA and other market requirements)
* Ensure Good Distribution Practice (GDP) compliance for commercial distribution, including qualification of third-party logistics providers, temperature excursion management, and returns
* Where applicable, integrate combination product and device quality requirements (e.g., 21 CFR Part 4) for drug-device presentations
* Develop and lead risk-based quality oversight of CDMOs, contract testing laboratories, and other GMP suppliers, including qualification, audits, and performance management.
* Negotiate and maintain commercial Quality Agreements and ensure adherence by Kailera and its partners
* Use independent judgment to resolve highly complex or novel quality issues, such as major deviations, OOS investigations, and supply disruptions, balancing patient safety, compliance, and supply continuity
* Direct cross-functional, multidisciplinary teams across Technical Operations, Supply Chain, Regulatory, and external partners to resolve quality events and implement improvements
* Build, lead, and develop a high-performing GMP Quality team as Kailera scales to commercial operations, including organizational design, hiring, and succession planning
* Drive followership by leading with trust, understanding, and adaptability; coach managers and team members, recognize contributions, and foster a culture of quality, accountability, and psychological safety
* Manage GMP Quality budget and resources, including the use of external consultants and auditors

 

**Required Qualifications:**

* 12+ years of GMP experience in the FDA-regulated pharmaceutical or biotechnology industry (or 10+ years with an advanced degree), including significant experience supporting commercial products
* Demonstrated success leading quality activities for product registration and commercial launch, including PPQ and PAI/PLI readiness
* 5+ years of people leadership experience, including building and developing teams
* Expert knowledge of cGMP and GDP requirements, including 21 CFR Parts 210, 211, and 11, EudraLex Volume 4 (including Annex 16), and ICH Q7, Q9, and Q10; working knowledge of 21 CFR Part 4 and DSCSA preferred
* Track record of successfully hosting or supporting FDA, EMA, and/or other health authority inspections
* Extensive experience leading quality oversight of CDMOs and contract laboratories, including audits and Quality Agreements
* Proficient in Veeva QualityDocs and Veeva QMS or a comparable electronic quality system
* Recognized expertise in GMP quality, with the judgment to give clear, risk-based quality advice that balances compliance with business needs
* Exceptional communication skills; tailors messages to executives, cross-functional partners, contract manufacturers, and health authorities, and explains the rationale behind decisions to build buy-in
* Proven ability to guide teams through complex change and ambiguity, anticipate problems before they escalate, and keep work focused on defined outcomes in a fast-paced, growing company
* Builds trusting relationships internally and externally, and navigates conflict through open dialogue and collaboration
* Brings creative, practical solutions to complex problems and encourages others to take calculated risks that challenge the status quo while maintaining compliance

 

**Education:**

* BA or BS degree in a scientific discipline required; advanced degree preferred

**For Full Time Roles:** This range represents the company's good-faith estimate of the salary at the time of posting. Actual pay may vary based on experience, skills, qualifications, location, and internal equity. We also offer comprehensive health coverage, flexible time off, paid holidays, and a year-end shutdown. Enjoy a monthly wellness stipend, generous 401(k) match, tuition reimbursement, commuter benefits, disability and life insurance, plus annual bonus opportunities and equity grants—because your well-being and future matter to us.

**EQUAL EMPLOYMENT OPPORTUNITY INFORMATION:**

Kailera Therapeutics, Inc. is an Equal Opportunity Employer that does not discriminate on the basis of actual or perceived race (including traits historically associated with race, such as hair texture and protective hairstyles), color, creed, religion (including religious dress and grooming practices), national origin, ancestry, citizenship status, age (40 and over), sex or gender (including pregnancy, childbirth, pregnancy-related conditions, and lactation), gender identity or expression (including transgender status), sexual orientation, marital status, military service and veteran status, physical or mental disability, genetic information, reproductive health decisions, domestic victim status, political affiliation, or any other characteristic protected by applicable federal, state, or local laws and ordinances.

This role connects application consulting with security and controls: you will help clients assess their needs, integrate safeguards into cloud-enabled processes, and support adoption across platforms such as Workday, Salesforce, and Microsoft Dynamics 365. You will help organizations manage technology risk while improving how their applications support day-to-day operations.
 
 
As a Director, you will set the direction for this work, cultivate executive client relationships, and identify opportunities to expand services where transformation programs call for integrated controls. You will guide multiple engagements, make decisions informed by program performance and emerging technology, and develop future leaders through coaching and candid feedback. Working across disciplines, you will connect platform architecture, application delivery, and risk perspectives while balancing commercial priorities with professional standards. Your leadership will foster an inclusive environment where people and technology contribute to client outcomes, reflecting PwC’s commitment to integrity and thoughtful service.

* Setting strategic direction for program risk and quality across business application transformations, aligning implementation, security, and controls priorities with client objectives
* Directing risk assessments and quality reviews across application projects, using business data analytics and performance measures to identify delivery gaps and guide corrective action
* Overseeing the design and integration of application access controls, automated monitoring, and compliance processes within cloud solutions such as Workday, Salesforce, and Microsoft Dynamics 365
* Guiding recovery of application security and controls work on large projects, coordinating resources, documentation, and technical consultation to address implementation challenges
* Shaping governance for SaaS security posture management and AI-enabled application integrations, including Model Context Protocol security, through research and the use of digital tools
* Leading teams through software implementation, user training, and ongoing support, coaching emerging leaders and adapting plans based on feedback and operational needs
* Cultivating executive client relationships and developing business opportunities by translating technical risks, transformation progress, and proposed solutions into recommendations for decision-makers
* Upholding professional standards while coordinating project delivery across disciplines, assessing technology performance, and encouraging inclusive collaboration between people and AI-enabled tools

 
What You Must Have

* At least 9 years of experience

* Directing security and controls strategy across cloud business application transformations and multiple client engagements
* Leading application security and access control design for Workday, Salesforce, or Microsoft Dynamics 365 implementations
* Integrating automated controls into business processes and monitoring their performance throughout technology implementations
* Overseeing application security and controls project recovery for large technology implementations

card.title: Senior Manager, US Quality Operations
card.description:
Xona is the navigational intelligence company bringing real-time, centimeter-level certainty to any device, anywhere on Earth.

With Pulsar – the world’s most advanced PNT satellite infrastructure in Low Earth Orbit – Xona will offer a future-proof, backwards-compatible global positioning system optimized for absolute precision, superior power, and robust protection.

As production grows, we need clear evidence that each spacecraft meets its requirements and a quality system that helps teams find and resolve risks early.

We are looking for a **Senior Manager, Quality Operations** to lead US quality for satellite buses and payloads from incoming material through building, test and acceptance. You will build a pragmatic system and lead engineers and inspectors close to the floor. You have independent authority to hold work or withhold readiness concurrence and to escalate unresolved mission risk. This is a hands-on leadership role in a fast-moving, dynamic environment.

**What you will do:**
=====================

* Lead US quality engineers and inspectors across supplier, receiving, production and test coverage. Set training, inspection points and delegated authority.
* Own fit-for-stage quality controls for document and configuration records, serial and lot traceability, calibration, nonconformances, corrective action and acceptance packages.
* Define risk-based controls for critical characteristics and supplier parts. Work with Supply Chain on qualifications, escapes, containment and verified corrective action.
* Make quality status visible through yield, repeat defects, escapes, NCR aging and acceptance-record completeness. Use trends to improve controls with Manufacturing and Engineering.
* Own the quality hold and escalation process. Engineering owns technical disposition; Quality evaluates controls and evidence and concurs on release.
* Concur independently on quality evidence at acceptance and flight readiness reviews. Escalate residual risk despite schedule pressure; partner with Engineering on reliability and mission risk.
* Align common requirements with the Canada Quality Lead and feed ground defects and on-orbit anomalies into later builds.

**What we are looking for**
===========================

* 8+ years in quality engineering or quality management for aerospace, defense or similarly complex hardware, including 3+ years directly leading engineers, inspectors or specialists through production and test.
* Experience building a usable QMS and leading teams through supplier escapes, nonconformances, root cause and corrective action.
* Independent judgment, strong technical communication and the ability to separate Engineering disposition from Quality release concurrence.
* Working knowledge of configuration control, risk-based inspection, process capability and cross-functional investigations.
* Bachelor’s degree in engineering, materials science, physics or a related technical field, or equivalent quality leadership experience in complex hardware.

**For U.S. Roles:** To comply with U.S. Government space technology export regulations, applicant must be a U.S. citizen, lawful permanent resident of the United States (i.e. Green Card holder), or other protected individual as defined by 8 U.S.C. 1324b(a)(3).

**For U.K. Roles:** To comply with U.K. regulations, this role requires Baseline Personnel Security Standard (BPSS) checks, and successful candidates must be eligible to obtain UK Security Clearance (SC).

**For Canada Roles:** Successful candidates must obtain and hold a security clearance at the reliability status level, and pass security assessment for the Canadian Controlled Goods Program (CGP) and ITAR.

We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, or veteran status.

Compensation Range: $180K - $230K
